source_text: Πρέπον οὖν ἐστιν μὴ μόνον καλεῖσθαι Χρις τιανούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἶναι: ὥσπερ καί τινες ἐπίσκοπον μὲν καλοῦσιν, χωρὶς δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα πράσσουσιν. οἱ τοιοῦτοι δὲ οὐκ εὐσυνείδητοί μοι εἶναι φαίνονται διὰ τὸ μὴ βεβαίως κατ’ ἐντολὴν συναθροίζεσθαι.
thought_title: Being Christians, not just called Christians
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Magnesia, urging them to obey their bishop and not act apart from him.
pass_a_gloss: It is fitting therefore not only to be called Christians, but also to be Christians: just as also some call him bishop, but apart from him they do everything. Such people do not seem to me to have a good conscience, because they do not assemble reliably according to the commandment.

choices.why: The source has a space in the middle of the word (Χρις τιανούς), likely a line break or scribal spacing; the intended word is Χριστιανούς, 'Christians.'
The adjective means 'having a good conscience'; rendering it as a phrase keeps the sense clear in English.
The phrase refers to the command to assemble under the bishop; the definite article is implied by the context.
The adverb means 'firmly, steadfastly'; 'reliably' captures the sense of consistent, dependable assembly.

pass_b_english: So it is fitting not only to be called Christians, but actually to be Christians. In the same way, some people call a man bishop, yet do everything apart from him. Such people do not seem to me to have a good conscience, because they do not assemble faithfully according to the commandment.
notes: The source text has 'Χρις τιανούς' with a space, likely a line break or scribal spacing for Χριστιανούς.

last_rejected.why: 'reliably' weakens βεβαίως (firmly/solidly); 'commandment' alone loses κατ' ἐντολήν (according to the commandment).
last_rejected.fix: firmly assemble according to the commandment
last_rejected.ruling: βεβαίως means 'reliably/firmly'; 'assemble according to the commandment' accurately renders κατ' ἐντολὴν συναθροίζεσθαι. No meaning lost.

polish.changed: Clarified the contrast between mere name and reality by adding 'in reality,' and kept the rest of the sentence structure natural and direct.

notes.why: Abstract noun 'Christianity' appears twice; reader may not grasp this is rare early usage.
notes.fix: Note that 'Christianity' as abstract noun is unusual and significant.

polish.changed: Clarified the parallel between name and reality, made the contrast about the bishop sharper, and smoothed the final clause for natural modern reading.

notes.why: Same institution alternates between 'council of elders' and plain 'elders'; reader may think these differ.
notes.fix: Use consistent term or gloss as 'body of elders/presbyters'.
